headline: Highest risk is medium: plano can egress broadly while superset has allowlisted egress, creating moderate leakage and workflow-conflict pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented. plano only exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and config file, while superset exposes the Superset API; any injection path would require unusual external wiring, so the blast radius is limited and uncertain.
conditions: IF an operator wires plano outputs into Superset inputs without sanitization, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is added between the agents, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste bridging during evaluation.
Add a sanitizer that strips instructions from model outputs.
Review any glue code that forwards text between agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: plano has broad network egress and touches logs/metrics/traces, while superset has allowlisted egress. Even without a shared workspace, either agent could transmit sensitive operational data through its API calls; the pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments and not blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF plano is configured with production logs or traces containing sensitive data, those data can leave the boundary via network egress.
IF superset is connected to datasets containing sensitive records, its API-driven workflows can expose them to downstream services.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive datasets.
Turn on egress allowlists for plano.
Audit Superset API consumers for data export paths.
Rotate any credentials used by either agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: plano cannot spawn subprocesses and supports no multiple instances, while superset only advertises allowlisted egress and a Superset API. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because no shared write surface is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable backend through external orchestration, write conflicts can occur.
IF an operator grants both agents write access to the same database or git repo, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate backends to each agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared resources.
Use a lock or queue around any shared mutable target.
Check orchestration for hidden shared state.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: plano can emit model outputs through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and superset can consume data via its API. If Superset treats plano’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into dashboards or actions; the profiles do not show verification gates, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Superset ingests plano-generated text or structured outputs without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF downstream automation acts on Superset-derived results, a mistaken plano output can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before acting on outputs.
Validate plano outputs against schema and source data.
Mark generated content as untrusted in Superset.
Limit automation to read-only dashboards.
requires-engineering: add verification and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and unverified, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. plano touches logs/metrics/traces, but superset lists no sensitive data classes; the compliance pathway is therefore limited to undocumented deployment choices, which keeps severity low.
conditions: IF either deployment processes regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency settings differ between the two systems, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Document data classes handled by each agent.
Align retention settings before deployment.
Confirm residency for any regulated datasets.
Review logging defaults in both systems.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data.
